raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year as I sit here planning.

---

*Well, I've been farming these 7.5 mu for thirty years now, since I was nineteen. My wife and I handle most everything ourselves — just the two of us in the household, so I can't be too ambitious. I know what works on this land and I don't change much unless I have a good reason.*

*Here's how I split things up: 5 mu stays on the wheat-maize rotation like most folks around here, and the other 2.5 mu I keep in cotton. The wheat-maize gives us grain for the year and some to sell, and the cotton is my cash crop — it's more work but the price per mu is better when it goes well. I wouldn't put more than 2.5 mu in cotton though, because the picking in autumn is brutal with just two of us. Even 2.5 mu stretches us thin during harvest, and I'll probably pay a neighbor's daughter or two to help for a few days.*

### Wheat (5 mu)

*I plant wheat around October 10th, after the maize comes off. I use the Jimai 22 variety — saved seed from last year, same as everyone around here. Before planting I run the rotovator through, spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, and sow with the seed drill. That's roughly 6 kg N as base.*

*In March when it greens up, I check the field. If it looks thin I'll topdress earlier; normally I wait until jointing in late March or early April and put down about 20-22 kg of urea per mu — that's around 10 kg more N. Total N comes out to maybe 16 kg per mu. The extension guy at the station says 15 is enough but I've always done a little more, and my yields are steady.*

*Irrigation — I water three times with the well: once in late November before the ground freezes (winter watering), once at jointing when I topdress, and once at grain-filling in May. Electricity for pumping runs about 20 yuan per mu per watering, so that's 60 yuan per mu just for water. If it rains well in spring I might skip the jointing one, but usually not.*

*Expecting around 420 kg per mu. Last year I got 440, year before was 400 because of that dry spell in April.*

### Maize (5 mu, after wheat)

*This is the tight part. Wheat combine comes through in early-to-mid June, and within a week I've got to get maize in the ground or I lose days at the back end. I use no-till direct seeding — the seed planter goes right into the wheat stubble. Zhengdan 958 hybrid, buy fresh seed every year.*

*I put down compound fertilizer with the planter — about 35 kg per mu of 15-15-15, plus I'll topdress urea at the big trumpet stage end of July, maybe 20 kg urea per mu. Total N around 14 kg. Maize doesn't need as much fuss as wheat once it's up.*

*For water — depends on the rainfall. Normal summer with the monsoon I might not irrigate at all. Dry year I'll water once at tasseling. Usually I plan for one irrigation and hope I don't need it.*

*Yield I expect around 480 kg per mu. Maize usually does better than wheat for me.*

### Cotton (2.5 mu)

*Cotton I plant late April, around the 20th when soil is warm enough. I plow this ground deeper before planting — cotton wants a loose seedbed. Buy hybrid seed, it's not cheap, about 60 yuan per mu for seed.*

*Base fertilizer is 30 kg of compound plus maybe 15 kg of urea worked in — cotton likes potassium too, so sometimes I add a bag of potassium sulfate. Then I topdress urea at budding in late June and again at flowering in mid-July. Total N around 13 kg per mu, and I put more K on cotton than on the grains.*

*Pesticides — this is where cotton eats your budget. I spray for aphids early, then bollworm through summer, probably 5-6 sprays total. I try to watch the field and only spray when I see the damage building, but you can't wait too long with bollworm. Herbicide once before planting.*

*Irrigation twice usually — once at budding, once at boll-filling. Picking starts in September and runs through October, multiple picks. This is where I'll need to hire — maybe 5-6 days of hired labor during peak picking.*

*Yield I expect around 240 kg lint per mu. Price has been okay lately but it jumps around.*

### What I'm watching this year

*The main thing I'm nervous about is the diesel and fertilizer prices — if urea goes up much more I might cut back a little on the wheat topdress. And the well water cost keeps creeping up with electricity. If we get a dry spring I'll have to water more and that eats into whatever cotton earns. But I've lived through worse — 2013 was harder than anything we've seen recently.*
